answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying reputation to costly, verifiable work rather than to account count: each agent must complete attested tasks whose results are checked by independent peers, so creating many fake identities gains no extra trust. Like light through a prism, one real record is split into separate checks — history, stake, and peer review — and only identities that pass all three earn spending rights. A flood of new accounts is then just a plume of noise in a nebula of claims, visible but weightless, because no history backs it.
